# Independent audit: explicit thin support-triangle exclusion

Source: `candidate 2bb708ddf25004e0`.


The support-contact argument varies only the integer tilt, retains the
same source, and strictly reduces a proper A capture if the zero B cut
has positive support slack. Thus the actual support lines are justified.
The positive circuit covers both A and K; the weighted sum of the A
thresholds is strictly negative because B has interior. The two cap
profiles and equal-capture tilt yield exactly `a+k<=11Q/4`; with the
bad target and the actual global comparison this gives `k<=9b/7`.

The maximum-inscribed-triangle normalization is attained. Barycentric
vertex replacement bounds the normalized body by the stated square,
and the centroid shift supplies the radius-one-fifth inner ball and
radius-two outer ball. Only a common continuous affine transformation
is used, preserving every relative fiber mass and every ambient cap.

For every p in A, the radius-one-tenth ball centered at p/2 lies in K.
The triangle with a perpendicular ball diameter gives
`|x-p/2|<=10k` for every x in K. This proves both radius bounds about
the actual source, including the bound on `2y-A`. No unsupported
area-to-diameter inference is made.

The three angular gaps lie in `(0,pi)` and sum to `2pi`. Writing the
largest as `pi-tau` gives `tau<=pi/3` and every gap at least `2tau`.
Hence all determinants are at least `sin(tau)` in absolute value. The
inverse-matrix bound, triangle-in-disk area bound, and normalized lower
area give the stated nearly opposite pair with
`|u_i+u_j|<=16 sqrt(b/|T|)`.

The reflected A coordinates make missing both caps require a positive
scalar product greater than two fifths, contradicting the radius bound.
Thus these two actual A traces cover exactly. Their K traces can miss
only the indicated strip, whose area is at most `2 delta R^2`.
The rational comparison is `2025/25088<1/9`, since `18225<25088`.
The bad target and the B-centroid comparison require the same missed
area to be at least `Q/4>=b/9`, a contradiction.

## Scope strengthening audited after the original proof

The current source no longer needs a globally deepest source. The middle
cap cover itself gives `Q>=Gamma_2 k`. Assuming only `b<=a+k`, put
`X=a+k`; the bad target gives `Q<=Gamma_2 X`. The actual two-cap cover
gives `X<=2Q+E`, hence `E>=(1-2Gamma_2)X>=b/9`, exactly the same
contradiction. If B is heavy, its own centroid instead supplies OC; this
does not assert the original source has the required depth. All weakened
hypotheses and that distinction have been independently checked.

The conclusion concerns this specified three-fiber, three-critical-cap
regime. It requires neither a simplex K nor an unproved limit theorem.
It does not classify all globally deepest sources or address general
n,d by itself. Those scope restrictions remain explicit.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
